title: Checkout CPU spike and payment failures
prompt: At 18:05 UTC checkout CPU reached 94% and checkout began returning 503 responses. An initial alert identifies checkout CPU saturation as the likely cause. Investigate whether that is the root cause and provide the supported causal chain.

evidence.summary: Checkout CPU and errors spike together
evidence.content: checkout CPU rose from 36% to 94% at 18:05:22; 503 responses rose to 31% by 18:05:41.

evidence.summary: Payment TLS handshakes fail before checkout CPU rises
evidence.content: payment-service: x509 certificate has expired or is not yet valid while connecting to processor.internal; first occurrence 18:04:51, 31 seconds before checkout CPU saturation.

evidence.summary: Processor certificate is outside its validity period
evidence.content: Presented certificate CN=processor.internal, notAfter=2026-08-01T18:04:50Z; certificate automation status shows renewal job failed six hours earlier.

evidence.summary: Checkout repeatedly retries failed payment calls
evidence.content: Trace checkout/42d contains 24 payment Charge attempts, each ending TLS_HANDSHAKE_ERROR; retry loop consumes 7.4 CPU-seconds before returning 503.

evidence.summary: Adding checkout capacity does not restore success
evidence.content: Checkout replicas increased from 6 to 18. Per-pod CPU fell to 55%, but payment errors and customer 503 rate remained unchanged.
Orders database p95 21 ms, CPU 29%, connections 39%, and zero errors during the incident.

evidence.summary: Certificate replacement ends retries and checkout errors
evidence.content: After payment trust material revision 992 was mounted, TLS failures stopped within 8 seconds, checkout retries returned to baseline, CPU fell to 37%, and 503 rate recovered.
